description.narrative: PROPOSAL FOR AN INSTITUTIONAL DEVELOPMENT FUND GRANT Project Manager for AADLC It is proposed that AADLC should identify and otherwise support a Project Manager in Training to oversee contracts with vendors. AADLC will be responsible for all aspects of his appointment - salary, office, etc. To support this person and to ensure the shortest possible learning period, it is proposed that a seasoned project manager be seconded, through the IDF Grant, to support AADLC for a period of 24 months. The objective is to ensure that there is a transfer of knowledge between thee AADLC-appointed project manager and the IDF-seconded seasoned project manager. Training in Small Business Management To enable AADLC to play its now enhanced role, the Association will be offered four (4) capacity building activities to be delivered by international consultants hired for this purpose through the IDF Grant. The areas of capacity building on which the training will focus will be Leadership training, Market development and scaling up initiatives, Proposal writing, Enterprise management and entrepreneurship, Strategic planning for centers. Specialized Training for Information Technology Specialists IT Specialists in Africna GDLN Centers will play a much more central role in facilitating the work of the Project Manager under the new contracts with vendors. Effectively the ITs will help each center to interact effectively with the centrally located Project Manager. To do this effectively, the ITs will need to upgrade their skills in Network Management. Accordingly, two training events will be organized specially for the ITs, focusing on the technical skills needed to bridge and otherwise manage communication to support audio and video communication for training events. Equipment for Bridging It is expected that for each of the Centers to provide bridging services, a limited number of equipment will have to be added at each site. Ten percent of the costs of these new equipments will be provided under the IDF. The Development Objectives of the proposed IDF grant is to strengthen the organizational and management capacity of the Association of African Distance Learning Centers (AADLC) to ensure it effectively performs essential functions on behalf of its members for capacity building and knowledge sharing in development. These functions include the development of an efficient working structure, including a strategy and implementation plan that will allow AADLC to be the main point of contact for relations with the World Bank, to support the expansion of the network in Africa and manage membership, business relations and development, advocacy, marketing and communications.
